title: PDF Workflow Checklist for Reliable Document Conversion
description: Follow a practical checklist for preparing PDFs, choosing the right output, and verifying quality after conversion.
author: Converigo

sections.title: Check the source file
sections.content: A clean source PDF is easier to convert and less likely to produce formatting issues. Make sure the file opens correctly and contains the pages you intend to preserve.

sections.title: Choose the output format carefully
sections.content: If you need easy sharing, JPG or PNG may be helpful. If you need layout fidelity, choose a format that preserves page structure better.

sections.title: Verify the result
sections.content: After conversion, confirm that text, images, and page order still look correct. A quick preview often catches problems before the output is shared.

faq.question: Do PDF conversions always preserve formatting?
faq.answer: They usually preserve the main structure, but some visual details may vary depending on the target format.

faq.question: Which format should I use for sharing?
faq.answer: PDF is often ideal for sharing documents, while JPG or PNG are better when you need image-based outputs.

faq.question: Should I convert scanned PDFs differently?
faq.answer: Sometimes. Scanned files may need extra review, especially if text recognition or image quality matters.
